Interface design · Qt Widgets · V3

MetaTV, redrawn

Every screen here was rendered by PyQt6, not drawn in a design tool. If it is in a picture, the engine can already draw it.

Engine Qt 6.11.1 Library 491,624 real titles Palettes 3 neutrals × 6 accents Decisions all settled

What Qt can render

Measured, not recalled — each feature applied to an identical widget, rendered twice, and diffed by text metrics or by pixels.

Ten of the eleven things a modern interface needs are supported. The one real loss is depth — no shadows, no blur, no opacity — so elevation here is built from layered surfaces and hairlines instead.

The constraint that matters least

The channel list is not styled by CSS at all. ChannelRowDelegate paints every row with QPainter, where none of the dropped features apply. The surface that matters most is the least constrained.

The one to remember

Qt does not clip a child widget to its parent's border-radius. It looks like it does if the parent's stylesheet is unscoped, because the radius cascades onto the child. Scope it with #objectName and a square corner bleeds straight through. Rounded posters must be pre-rounded into the pixmap.

Foundations

Five scales and a palette, each chosen against a constraint the engine imposes.

Type

Today's scale has nine steps with seven inside a 6px band, so FONT_SM and FONT_HEADING differ by 5px and read as the same size. Seven steps, none closer than 2px, with weight carrying the rest.

Spacing and radius

Surfaces

With box-shadow dropped, elevation is a seven-step ramp plus a one-pixel hairline. Real shadows stay available through QGraphicsDropShadowEffect — keep them for things that genuinely float, since each one costs a graphics effect.

Colour

All three neutrals stay — Midnight, Graphite and Daylight. Accent becomes a separate axis rather than something baked into each palette, which it half-way already is (accent_color is in your config today). Three neutrals and six hues describe eighteen looks from nine definitions.

Each hue is solved rather than picked: saturation held in a muted band, then lightness walked until it clears 5.5:1 as text and its on-accent foreground clears 4.5:1 as a fill. Red and green need genuinely different values per mode, so each hue stores a pair rather than one colour the theme tints.

Separately, three existing tokens never reached AA and drive 11–13px text at 159 call sites. The current contrast suites cannot see them because those rules declare a colour and no background.

Icons

Material Symbols, which is the set you were thinking of. Monochrome, one stroke weight, and it solves a problem the current emoji marks have: emoji render differently on every platform and cannot take a theme colour. These are glyphs, so they inherit the text colour like any other character.

The three kind marks were chosen by rendering candidates at the sizes the row actually paints them, not by name: movie for films, tv for series — live_tv and smart_display both carry a play triangle and read as a play button — and sensors for live, because satellite_alt collapses into scribble at 15px.

The window

The menu bar stays visible for now. Split and Tools are in the header; Settings appears once, at the foot of the sidebar.

Rows

Three rules, in order of how much they matter.

Nothing moves when a row is selected. The action slot at the right is always reserved and only painted on hover or when the row is current. Row geometry is computed by a function that takes no state argument, so a shift is not something to remember to avoid — it is unrepresentable. That is also what makes the design work on touch: "current" is reachable by tap and by keyboard, where hover is not.

Kind is structural. Movie, series and live each get a mark and their own meta line, because they do not have the same facts — a series shows seasons and episodes, a live channel shows its category and a square tile it will actually have art for.

Only render what exists. Quality appears on the 6.6% of rows that have a value and nowhere else. Ratings are gone from the row entirely — they are not objective, and in this library the top of the range is a wall of identical 10.0s.

Reserve versus render

An action slot is reserved because every row can be acted on. A quality slot is not, because 93.4% of rows have nothing to put in it. Reserve what is always true; render what is sometimes true.

Sidebar

It stays a working surface. Clicking a section header expands it in place and never replaces the centre view; the → arrow is the deliberate escalation to a full view, and clicking an item acts on the item.

The problem was never the metaphor, it was allocation. Your saved layout reads alerts 173 · recommended 113 · queue 403 · favorites 26 · history 91 — Queue gets 4.4× what History gets, and Alerts subdivides 173px four ways with a scrollbar in each. Three mechanisms fix it: no nested scrollbars, content-aware minimums, and a news boost so a section widens when it has something to say.

A collapsed section now carries news rather than a count, because a count is inventory and +9 eps is news.

Sections still stretch

+N more is not a cap. It is what appears when the allocated height runs out — drag a section taller and it renders more rows. The minimum is a floor, never a ceiling.

Details

The action architecture is unchanged, because it was already right: a slim rail over the poster's left edge, the Watched badge on the poster corner, a full-width primary row, and the sentiment trio at the right of the secondary row. Only the visual language is new.

Similar titles moved to the bottom and gained a header row: a count, a posters / list toggle, and ⤢ to open the cascading-column overlay. It shows a handful rather than all eighteen, because the overlay is where you go to actually browse them — the pane only needs to say "there are more, here is the door". Posters keep their names; the posters alone were prettier and less useful.

Also-available stays chips, as it is today. That matters at real scale: Kraven The Hunter has 65 versions across 20 regions and Nickelodeon has 94 across 32. Grouping by region and collapsing that region's qualities onto the chip turns sixty-five lines into eight.

Decisions

All settled. Recorded here so the reasoning survives the decision.

O1The view switcher — one refinement, one new option

Option A now fills the whole active section rather than floating an inset chip inside it. The track keeps its hairline dividers and its own outer radius carries the end corners, so the selection reads as part of the control instead of sitting on top of it.

Option D folds the switcher into the brand. MetaTV recedes to a small label and the current view becomes the large, clickable line beneath it — the whole thing costs one corner of the header and no horizontal space at all. It does hide the other four views behind a click, which is the same objection that applies to any dropdown; the difference is that it always shows where you are, which a collapsed segmented control does not.

Suggestion. Settled — A is the default; D ships alongside it as an interface option in Settings.
O2Filters as chips

Settled — shipping behind the existing panel so you can switch back if the chips lose the overview.

O3Language badge fill

Settled — Filled / Outline / Off, default Filled.

On the preferred-language setting you remembered: it is real, but it is not what you think it is. metadata_tmdb_language is an open text field in Settings (settings_dialog.py:433) — so the UI precedent exists — but it sets the language TMDb metadata is fetched in, not which variant appears in results. There is no preferred_language anywhere in the code or in the entire git history.

What does exist, usefully: the series monitor already records a language per tracked title (language: EN, language: SC in its state), so the notion of 'which variant of this title' is already modelled per title. A global preference would be the missing piece, and it could seed from those choices rather than starting empty.

O4Configurable details layout

Moved to the roadmap. Sections are collapsible with remembered state, which covers the immediate need; hide / add / reorder is its own slice.

O5UI face

Settled — Inter, Latin subset, regular and semibold. Largest x-height of the candidates and clearest at 11–12px, which is where most of this interface lives.
